Parents are urged to reconsider the screen time limits they have set as their children return to school. Some suggest that stressed parents may have adopted a more relaxed approach to screen time during the summer holidays, but when the new school term begins, this practice could have serious adverse effects on their children.

In addition, experts say the previously recommended daily two-hour limit is outdated, and parents should adopt a more refined approach based on the "5 Cs"……

CNET points out that when children stay at home all day, parents experience greater stress and therefore rely more on electronic devices to keep them occupied.

Experts say this situation may not necessarily be a problem.

However, if adjustments are not made after children return to school, doing so could put them at risk.

Child development experts point out that excessive media use may lead to declining academic performance, weakened ability to control attention, and impaired cognitive abilities.

If you are unsure how much screen time is appropriate for children of different ages, you can refer to the guidelines provided by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP).

Apple's built-in "Screen Time" and other parental control features have received major upgrades in iOS 27.
